feeds_accelerator_ids.locator: Bethke and Wagner (arXiv:2208.11076), section on PETRA; Klein and Yoshida (arXiv:0805.3334), Table 1 and the text on HERA's injection
feeds_accelerator_ids.note: PETRA is the last stage before HERA: protons LINAC III, DESY III, PETRA (40 GeV), HERA; electrons LINAC II, DESY II, PETRA (12 GeV), HERA (Klein and Yoshida, Table 1: "Protons Source RFQ LINAC III DESY III PETRA HERA Ep 20 keV 750 keV 50 MeV 8 GeV 40 GeV 920 GeV Electrons Ee Source 150 keV LINAC II 450 MeV PIA 450 MeV DESY II 7 GeV PETRA 12 GeV HERA 27.5 GeV"; "Initially the use of PETRA as a pre-accelerator caused some problems due to eddy-current effects in HERA proton magnets at low energies and for tight injection aperture."). Conflict: the DESY anniversary page says PETRA served "starting in 1986, as a preaccelerator for the even bigger HERA ring"; Bethke and Wagner, who describe the November 1986 shutdown and the rebuilding as PETRA-II, give 1990 and the end in 2007 (HERA ceased operation in June 2007). 1990, the paper's year, is used. The link ends with HERA's operation; PETRA's later roles (synchrotron radiation from 1995, PETRA III from 2009) are outside the Atlas scope (A26).
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: After its shutdown as particle collider in November 1986, PETRA came back to life in 1990 as PETRA-II, where it served as pre-accelerator for the electron-proton collider HERA until 2007.

summary.plain: DESY's 2.3-kilometre electron-positron ring in Hamburg, which collided beams from 1978 to 1986. Experiments there (TASSO, MARK J, JADE, PLUTO, CELLO) found the first direct evidence of the gluon in three-jet events in 1979.
summary.technical: PETRA e⁺e⁻ storage-ring collider, 2304 m circumference, beam energy up to 23.39 GeV (centre-of-mass up to about 46.8 GeV); first collisions September 1978, final collider shutdown 3 November 1986. Four collision regions: TASSO, MARK J, JADE and PLUTO (replaced by CELLO in March 1980). Later reused as HERA pre-accelerator and as the PETRA III light source.
